text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab S 10.5-Inch Tablet (16 GB, Titanium Bronze) I love this tablet and, if it weren't for the battery life and how long it takes to recharge, I would give it 5 stars. The tablet itself is beautiful, thin, lightweight and works beautifully. I have had mine since the beginning of September 2014, and I have only had to reboot it twice since then (due to errors, I mean). The display is beautiful. The sound is quite good, for a tablet. And now that Samsung has allowed it to upgrade to Lollipop, I can run most of my new apps from my 32 gb SD Card and this leaves me a lot less nervous about running out of memory. Though, I still find the 16 GB HD a bit on the tight side overall.

My previous tablet was a Toshiba Excite AT305T16. It was my first tablet, but I still could tell how slow it was. And it constantly needed to be rebooted. Everything kept getting bound up on it. Not so with this Samsung. It is quick, it stays fresh, and it just plain performs. Which is all we ask for, right? I will be buying more Samsung products in the future, I think. Those guys really know and deliver quality. Now, if they could just improve the battery and be a bit more generous with the on-board memory.

UPDATE: I have downgraded my review by one star. I have owned this tablet since August of 2014. And, although I still enjoy it, I am now running out of memory and, even though I have a 64gb sd card attached, I am finding it increasingly challenging and frustrating to manage the remaining space. While many of the apps can be moved to the SD card, most of them can't. And the apps themselves are becoming larger and larger overall. And, to make matters worse, suddenly, I can no longer update many of my apps residing on the SD card, unless I move them back to the internal storage first. This is too laborious and time consuming and I haven't found a fix for it yet. Also, suddenly I can no longer move PDF files onto the SD card either. Other types of files can be moved as before, but not the PDF files. Wondering if the tablet performed some sort of automatic system upgrade that may have triggered these issues. When I "upgraded" (and I use that term lightly, with tongue in cheek) from Kitkat to Lollipop, the tablet lost some very useful functions. So now I have to wonder why these problems are suddenly cropping up?
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab S 10.5-Inch Tablet (16 GB, Titanium Bronze)

text_fidelity_a:
3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD Prior to getting this NVR system, I had already started researching on POE switches. For some reason, I assumed all NVR cameras are POE. I knew this Dragon Touch NVR had no POE ports in the back, but it didn't matter because I had planned to use POE switches. If you're a newbie like me, here are some noteworthy things before you make your decision:

1. The four cameras in this set comes with four power adapters. I thought how nice of them to include this option. But as it turns out, this is NOT an option. You need to use the power adapters for each camera. I learned that getting POE switches is only half the battle, the other half is making sure the cameras are POE compatible. I didn't know that. I thought POE switches would allow me to get rid of power adapters to any camera, any brand. Sadly, this is not the case. So this Dragon Touch system is designed for wi-fi. You only need to hook up the power adapter to each camera. But the whole point of me going to NVR is to use ethernet for more dependable connections. You can still do that with this system, but you'll still need to connect the power adapters, so you're running two cables for each camera. Had I known that, I would not have gotten this system.

2. You can use other brand cameras with this NVR if the cameras are ONVIF. However, I'm betting they still need to be the non-POE kind. I'm trying to connect a H.View POE camera, but I'm getting a black screen. Dragon Touch said that model is not compatible. End of email. I had to follow up with "What POE cameras are compatible?" I'll update when they respond.

3. It goes without saying, but in case you don't know, you need to connect NVR to a monitor for viewing. The back of the NVR has options for VGA or HDMI out. Alternatively, you can view via their Homeviz app.

4. No hard drive is included, but a hard drive is not necessary for you to start learning, testing, and setting things up. You can live view without a hard drive, but to record you'll need to install a hard drive.

5. Lastly, I'll talk about the build quality of this system. The Dragon Touch is very professionally packaged, the NVR is small and light, but that's without a hard drive currently. The cameras feel real nice, has good heft to them. I am not going to subtract any stars because of my newbie assumptions. As a matter of fact, I'm learning that if you want NVR systems with POE cameras, they would be much more expensive than what you're paying here. If I can figure a way to run both ethernet and power adapters, I may end up using this system. However, I will subtract a star for the lack of info in their listing, and emails. A product like this should clearly state whether or not their cameras are POE, and whether or not the NVR can handle POE cameras. 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: 3MP Wireless Security Camera System, Dragon Touch 8CH NVR 4pcs WiFi Security Cameras Outdoor with Color Night Vision, AI Human Detection, Motion Alert, Remote Access, IP66 Waterproof Cameras, No HDD

text_fidelity_a:
Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology This is a cameras that is perfect for some but not something that everyone will find useful. The ideal user is someone who wants a simple to use digital camera that has the ability to instantly print the photo without dealing with a PC or conventional printer. This does a pretty good job of accomplishing that goal. But, if you’re looking for a more advanced point and shoot with lots of image features, this may not be your best option.

The camera itself feels very solid, but lacks a key digital camera feature: a view screen. At first glance may seem to be a major omission. But, this camera is designed to be a high-tech replacement for the old-style Polaroid instant cameras by instantly (well, relatively instantly) printing the photo on Zink paper. Note that the paper needs to be purchased separately, and is pretty much an essential component for using the camera. While you can store photos on an SD card, the camera is really designed to be used with the Zink paper.

Usage is very straightforward – it’s about as point and shoot as you can get. That’s great for those who don’t want to fiddle with any settings, but it does put some constraints on image quality. I’ve had about 20% of my photos so far turn out less than ideal due to improper focus, poor white balance, poor resolution and/or incorrect color registration. That’s my major complaint with this camera – the paper is costly, and when you have to toss (or at least not really like) one in five photos, the cost can add up.

The images are small – the paper is only 2 by 3 inches. On the plus side it has a peel and stick backing, so you can use the photos as “post-its” very easily. Again, this is keeping with the intent of the camera, so I won’t downgrade the rating due to the small photo size.

Other negatives for me is that the battery is not user-replaceable. I’ve had too many electronic products with built-in batteries that had to be trashed since the internal battery no longer held a charge. I’m also not fond of the lens cap. It’s very easy to take off (it’s held in place by magnets) but there’s no attachment to the camera, so it’s very easy to misplace.

But this does score well with regard to ease of use and fun. As a test of ease of use I handed this to my Mom who is technically challenged, to say the least. She had no problems snapping photos and loved having the image print right there. She’s never liked using a digital camera in the past due to difficulty using it and dealing with image files. This was right up her ally.

While I’ll drop the rating to 4 stars due to the image quality issues that can crop up, overall this is a unique camera. It’s not right for everyone, but if you’re looking to revisit the days of the Polaroid instant camera while staying in the digital world, this is well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

text_fidelity_a:
Otium Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earbuds 15H Playtime with Mic HD Stereo Sound Sweatproof in-Ear Earphoones Noise Cancelling Headsets Gym Running Workout Pink My Otium beats will be four years old in July. I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed.

🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them.

💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater.

🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]].

💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys.

🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips.

🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies.

🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars.

In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Otium Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earbuds 15H Playtime with Mic HD Stereo Sound Sweatproof in-Ear Earphoones Noise Cancelling Headsets Gym Running Workout Pink

Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a:
Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White We've been using an older first generation Portal and like it very much. I was not expecting to be so impressed with this one, but wow have they managed to improve almost everything about the original! It still has the very cool zoom-and-pan style camera feature that follows the subject, as well as all the fun filters and of course my kids' favorite, story time... but the polish and style of this unit is really premium. The speaker is fantastic and LOUD if you want it to be. The clarity and bass rivals my bookshelf speakers so well, sometimes the kids play music off it and I could have sworn they were using the speakers in the living room. But the biggest improvement over the previous generation is the ability to run off battery power and move around. The "portable portal" honestly makes so much sense, I wonder why the original stationary style ones came out first!
Make no mistake, it is NOT a tablet, it is not thin and won't fit in an attaché case nicely. It is wedge-shaped making it stand easily at an ideal angle, and even has a cut-out handle to pick it up and carry it to a better location for video chat. This is great for bringing it to wherever my kids happen to be congregating currently, and it can be put back up on the shelf when done to charge. Like the original Portals, it has Alexa built in and can act as an Echo for most things, however it is very tied into Facebook's ecosystem. That means that although it seems to run something akin to Android behind the scenes, this is NOT going to offer a standard App store, and even things like Youtube are not available for it (licensing issues with Google I'd suppose). However there is a browser, and you can navigate to YouTube and play it from the website just fine, although a proper app would be much easier to navigate. It does have Plex support, which I found interesting since I have a Plex server. I never thought I'd find Plex available where Youtube is not! Meanwhile, between Youtube in the browser, Amazon Music through Alexa and content on Plex, there are plenty of ways to make it a music streamer on that glorious better-than-it-should-sound speaker. And the camera works just as well if not better than the OG Portal!
Calls over FB Messenger or Whatsapp work well, and of course the camera / mic not only have a switch to toggle, but the camera has a physical cover that can slide over the lens in case you don't trust Facebook not to snoop. But that's another story.
All things considered, this is a solid product.
text_fidelity_b: Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White

Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc. I purchased a Lenovo Ideacentre AIO Y910 in December 2017 and it had a beautiful built-in Qualcomm bluetooth function. It worked great. I had my desktop paired with my Echo Dots and with Alexa could continue listening to movies/music/podcasts/youtube anywhere in my house away from the computer. Along came a Windows 10 update in March 2018 that disabled/removed the bluetooth function/drivers ENTIRELY. No roll backs/restores, or reinstallations brought it back. The internal bluetooth function was completely ruined and prevented from running. I was furious and microsoft support was zero help. I finally begrudgingly purchased this to do the same function. I'm angry I had to pay for something I already paid for my computer to have, and that I have to waste a USB spot for it, but it works, was truly plug and play, though the connecting of all my speakers/Echo Dots is more complicated that previously. For example, with the original bluetooth capabilities, I could chose to have one or both of the Dots automatically connect when bluetooth was enabled. I could have them play together or verbally tell Alexa to connect/disconnect. Now for some reason with this bluetooth, voice control doesn't work, Alexa can't disconnect (she will do it but then it automatically reconnects) and if one Dot is connected the other won't. I have to run back to my computer's bluetooth settings and pair/unpair and connect/disconnect each time I want to make a change. This is frustrating. If anyone knows of anyway to circumvent this or the original bluetooth death please let me know, I'd be forever grateful.

The range for the device is fine, I live in a 1200 sq ft two story townhome and there was no issue with my computer seeing the Dot in the bedroom or the Dot downstairs. Connections are strong.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red) This is a smart case - no bra needed.

UPDATE: Wrong, alas. I mean, it’s possible to make this case put your headphones to sleep – at least with the version of this case that I have – but it’s such a precise, finicky, painstaking endeavor that it’s nowhere near worth the effort. I’ve taken to using my case just like everybody else does: with the bra inside.

My guess is that what these third-party case makers need to do is what Apple did with the bra: rather than a couple of dime-sized round magnets, they need to put in long, thin magnets that will connect with the sensors in the earcups no matter where in the case they fall. The bra puts the headphones to sleep every time without fail and without the user having to spend several minutes massaging the headphones into just exactly the perfect position so that they’ll go to sleep, so it can be done; the third-party case manufacturers just haven’t yet figured out how Apple did it.

Anyways: I was dreading this case having an horrendous stench to it, based on several reviews I've read. I'm happy to report that while mine has a smell and it is kind of chemical-y, I find the smell neither strong nor entirely unpleasant. It's pretty mild, strength-wise (and I'm sensitive to such things) and I find the smell has a sort of fresh quality to it, despite its chemical nature. Lucky me, I guess. But this, like the Apple bra, is basically half a case. You need the bra to put the headphones to sleep, and this case to give them adequate protection. Hard to believe in this day and age, but there it is. I guess if Apple included a case with these that did everything necessary they would probably charge an additional $200 for it…
text_fidelity_b: co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red)

I also have the Liberty 2 Upgraded version, and while those are very good, these are clearly superior.

I did use the Soundcore app to update the firmware and enable LDAC: you'll definitely want to do this before you begin using them. Also, there are other settings on the app you might find useful.

They are also very comfortable to wear for long periods (I use them at my desk while working), and even using LDAC (which uses a lot more power) the battery lasts as long as I've needed so far. The case is nice and compact, and of course charges the earbuds quickly. The only thing I would grumble about (and now I'm being very fussy) is that I have to turn the earbuds over to get them into the right position for the case.

Another note: Anker was offering a "used like new" item for a much lower price, so I decided to try them. I'm very happy I did, since they really were just like a new product, seemed unused (probably a quick return). All the earpiece bits were new, of course.

Bose QuietComfort Noise Cancelling Earbuds-Bluetooth Wireless Earphones, Triple Black My family has tested out numerous noise canceling earbuds in the last six months, looking for the best ones to fit each member of our household. This set of earbuds was the universal favorite among every member of our family.

For one, the noise cancellation feature is absolutely the most effective noise cancellation we have found on earbuds. Even having it on silent, I was unable to discern individual words from my mom reading loudly to my two noisy children in the other room. With an audiobook playing, I really didn't notice anybody else being in the house, though I could hear them if I thought about it. With music, it was like they weren't there, someone can stand right next to me and talk to me and I can be blissfully unaware.

If you get overloaded from auditory stimulation easily and just need the world to stop making so much noise every so often, these are the earbuds to get.

The sound quality is extraordinarily good on audiobooks, rap music, metal music, and more peaceful and soothing ballads and classical. The base was not overwhelming, nor did the treble get screechy.

It fit my very small ears well, and fit my husband's ears well also, he has a much bigger ear canal size.

The one thing that we have both noticed is that these are also heavier than most of our other earbuds, however even with my ears feeling rather sensitive, it really didn't bother me because they are weighted nicely and fit so well.

Overall, while these could be improved by being slightly smaller and less heavy, these still beat out five other well-known brands in our household for both the noise cancellation and in audio quality.

text_fidelity_a:
APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) One of the main reasons I selected this model is the simplicity of a single battery cartridge design. My previous APC UPS units use spade connectors. I have limited use of my hands and fingers which makes it a challenge to use spade connectors so I was looking forward to the cartridge battery simplicity. When the product arrived I installed it as per the clear and easy to follow directions. But the UPS acted as if the battery was not connected and / or missing altogether. After spending a considerable time diagnosing the problem I finally removed the cartridge battery (Aaa-gain) to make a close inspection. I found there are two male blade connectors located within a pocket in the cartridge battery. Two female blade connectors are located in a protrusion inside the UPS unit battery compartment so as to self align and engage the male blades inside the pocket in the cartridge battery when the cartridge battery is installed and seated fully. One of the two male blade connectors is either missing or pressed in too deep to be reached by the mating coupling. I made a feeble attempt to tug at the stubby male blade sunk deep within the socket but gave up when I realized how stupid the situation is. This is a brand new product so why should I attempt to make a risky repair?

The problem as I see it is in attempting to get two flimsy electrical connectors to self align the first time every time all the time. If they had used common banana jacks instead of spade connectors it would only cost a penny more yet be so much more reliable.

As I write this I am awaiting a reply from APC. If APC will not take care of this problem then I will return my purchase to Amazon.com for a refund. I will follow up with the remedy after it is complete.
text_fidelity_b: APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately)

If you intend to use this as a fixed table lamp the cable issue will not be the problem for you that it is for me.

Second, the gooseneck is sensitive. If I bump a music stand with this light clamped to the shelf it will move far out of place. It's not stiff enough to hold if you do plan to use it with a music stand. For tables, bed stands, etc. it should work fine, though.

Here are some of the strengths: the lowest setting of illumination is perfect for stage use or if you want to read in bed without waking your partner up. At the highest setting it is definitely bright when lose in (about 1.5 meters), and - as Goldilocks said - the medium setting is just right.

Another feature is untethered to the charger this will operate for three hours at the brightest setting and half more than double that at the lowest. That means that if you are camping, on stage (or in front of a lectern) without a power source nearby you can still use it.

Finally, the included wall wart has a 2 Amp port for phones and tablets, as well as a 500mA port for charging this light. That is handy and all the more reason why the cable style for this lamp is a frustration - it could have easily been a five star product, and especially at the going price.

Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones

SIN SHINE - Compressed Air 3.0- Multi-Use Electric Air Duster for Cleaning Dust, Hairs, Crumbs, Scraps for Laptop, Computer, Replaces Compressed Air Cans (AD01-Black) I use canned dusters for a variety of purposes, from cleaning keyboards to cleaning up my electric shaver. These sometimes leave residue behind, so I was interested in trying this electric duster to see if it would cut down on residue and save money in the long run. I will confess that I was not very optimistic and thought it would be underpowered. However, it has proven to be as effective as a canned duster in cleaning keyboards and other equipment, without leaving any residue and without losing power like canned dusters tend to do as they get cold.

This device is smaller than a tea kettle and relatively light. It requires an AC outlet so it does need to be plugged in when you want to use it. I was hopeful I had missed something on the description and that there was a rechargeable battery but unfortunately this is not the case. This was me being hopeful, not a confusing write-up.

It comes with a few attachments to help direct the air flow over the surface of what you’re trying to clean. The most helpful attachment, to me, is the round nozzle, but all of them have their uses.

I took it to my office where we have an abundance of dirty keyboards that need to be cleaned, and I set to work. I was expecting it to do a mediocre cleaning job, but it gave me a very pleasant surprise and blew air with plenty of force to clean out the clumps of dust that collect under the keys. More importantly, though, the power didn’t diminish like what tends to happen with canned dusters as they get cold, and there was no problem with frost buildup either.

So far, this is proving to be a useful and helpful tool. It produces enough force to get the job done without losing power, and it leaves no residue behind.

Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

Though it is a good idea and it does accomplish its stated purpose it has a couple of shortcomings, the largest of which is the price.

The idea of this device is very simple - it has dividers where one can put a set of tablets, laptops, even cell phones, plug them all in and keep everything neat and tidy all while using a single wall outlet. The trade-off is the size of this unit, which takes up a fair amount of desk space. It takes up about as much space as a desktop computer.

The whole unit comes with 10 outlets on a heavy-duty power strip which slide-mounts on the back. The cables then run through the unit and under a plastic baffle and out the front where they can plug into the devices to which they correspond. The concept is fairly simple and straightforward, and the implementation works - you will have less desk clutter and the cords will be a lot less likely to get tangled and knotted. However, it does mean taking the unit apart to remove a cable should the need arise, though that’s simple enough.

The power cord is nice and long which is a good thing. This addresses and issue I have had in my specific configuration where the closest available outlet is across the room, out of each from most devices. Of course, with 10 outlets available on this unit that frees up a couple of the closer outlets.

The tray and base are made of heavy-grade plastic and should hold up to years of use. I have no issues with the construction or design of this thing.

This is an expensive piece of equipment - $200 retail as I write this. I’m sorry, but that is far higher than what is reasonable. I could see an asking price of maybe $65-$75 but beyond that is simply too much. Even the sale price here on Amazon is still too high. For the same price, a power strip with a large, heavy cardboard box would serve the same purpose. The price is the single biggest problem with this unit.

I have a very difficult time recommending this unit mainly because of the price. Cutting the price in half would still make it expensive but it would be close to reasonable. If decluttering your desk is the goal and you don’t mind spending a good bit of money on an organizational system this is not a bad choice.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Secure and Charge - AC Lockable Classroom Charging Station for Laptops & Tablets - Classroom Organization & iPad Charging Station - Up To 10 Devices Including iPads, Samsung Tablets & More

AERY PF8616 8”x6, Advanced Drawing Tablet with Pro Pen 8 & 8192 Level Eraser and Turntable Wheel Control with 24 Shortcuts & Accessories I had been looking at these types of drawing tablets and wanted to give this one a try. I'm not a professional, and I know that things like "lag" are sometimes a concern, but I personally didnt find excessive lag (not that I could notice, anyway). In fact, I found this to be very impressive in that regard for this price.

Installation was a breeze, simply download the apps and away you go. (I'm using a windows 10 system). I was able to immediately use the Penwalker thing on my main screen with nothing open (scribbling notes right across my screen, etc). Then I pulled open photos hoping and tried some simple scribbling- that's when I noticed that the touch sensitive nature of this system is really effective - pressure effects line weight, etc. The pens are lightweight, yet the pressure sensitivity gives them a certain "feel". I think I could get used to this.

Then I opened Clip Studio Paint Pro and just doodled for a moment. Alternating between brushes, fades, erasers, etc. Again, the "feel" is what impressed me most (in spite of the lightweight pens). There's function buttons identified right on the tablet, (everything appears to work as it should), and when you bring the pens tip within an inch or so of the tablets screen, you can use to pen like a mouse to position the cursor- then touch the screen to do your work. Same with the eraser end - turn the pen around and point the eraser end to the screen and position your cursor with it - then touch down to erase.

As an amateur, I've barely scratched the surface of this tablets capabilities, but I can already tell that it's going to be fun learning some new skills as I spend more time with this. For me, this one's a winner!

text_fidelity_a:
Alienware Alpha ASM100-4980 Console (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This review is going to be a bit difficult to write in that there is SO much to say about this system that different people might be interested in knowing about. I will attempt to be as brief, yet well rounded in my review as I can due to space constraints.

WHAT IS THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE (7980)?
In essence, what this unit is, is a complete Windows 8.1 PC unit with the ability to boot directly into Valve's Big Picture console interface of the Steam accounts immediately, or boot directly into Windows. No matter what, you have to be online to be able to the Steam Console because of the fact that in order to access your account, you have to be able to log in.

In order to log in, you have to be online. Big Picture mode can also be accessed through Windows. By pressing the icon for Steam on the desktop (which will take you directly into your Steam account) you can also access the Big Picture console interface by pressing the controller symbol in the top right corner of the window.

This console comes with Windows 8.1 which is a challenge in itself as the operating system has a lot of quirks and frustrations that come along with it no matter WHAT hardware it operates on. There is a bit of a learning curve with Windows 8.1 but it is worth taking the time to work with it, if you have never used it before.

The machine itself is very small- smaller than a PS3 unit. It has a cool alien head on the front of the machine that changes colors during different operations. You hook it up into your sound system through HDMI or Digital Optical Link, or into TV directly using HDMI.

The power cord is in two parts- it is 68 inches from the console to the AC adapter and 32 inches from the adapter to the plug. It also comes with a 6ft HDMI cable.

There is an HDMI IN so you can input HDMI sources to pass through this unit into your TV.

WHAT CAN YOU DO WITH THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE?
This machine is set up with the gamer in mind. It is very powerful and does play some of the highest demanding games on the market right now without any trouble. It is also set up with the console gamer in mind, specifically the Xbox crowd as it comes with a wireless Xbox 360 controller (which is already set up to work in Windows).

Many Playstation gamers as well as others are not fond of this controller. We did manage to set up a Playstation 3 controller using the Motion Joy and Pinnacle Profiler method that we downloaded from online. Motion joy is free, but Pinnacle Profiler is a one-time fee to download it (after a 20 day trial period).

CAN YOU PLAY OLDER PC GAMES ON THIS SYSTEM?
One of the concerns I had, which I am sure others out there might have is- "Can I play all of my older PC games on this unit as well as Steam games?" The answer is YES! All of our games (purchased through Gog.com previously) work beautifully on this system. That means you do not have to be connected to the internet to play them.

WHAT SHOULD YOU PLAN TO PURCHASE?
--Keyboard (I use Logtiech K400 wireless w/ touchpad on board I use for basic Windows stuff)
--Mouse (I use Marathon Mouse for games)
--DVD-ROM/CD-ROM USB drive (if you want to install anything using those)
--Wireless headphones if you want to use them for gaming

BLUETOOTH
I have a pair of Turtle Beach i30 wireless headphones that operate by bluetooth. I found conflicting information on their site as to whether this would work with Windows 8.1 or not, so I tried installing it.

Windows 8.1 has some idiosyncrasies with bluetooth and is notorious for causing problems in this area. When attempting to install my headphones with this system, the process somehow completely messed up the bluetooth operations in the system. It took me a couple of days to figure it all out, but with a lot of perseverance and some Free Ccleaner added for registry and system cleaning, I managed to get the bluetooth headphones to work beautifully.

This is not a console problem but a Windows 8.1 problem.

ARMA III
We ran this game with maxed out settings, this system ran 30fps smoothly and perfectly. (At the time of this review Arma III is a military simulator that has a very high graphics demand. It is one of the top most demanding games on the market at this time.)

Graphically it looks way better than anything from Modern Warfare.

IS THIS WORTH IT?
PROS
-completely functional PC in all aspects of Windows 8.1
-small physical footprint
-plays all levels of PC games very well
-comes with Xbox controller
-works with PS3 controller
-can get decent keyboard and mouse for very little extra money
-allows family gaming
-more convenient for limited space in living area
-will shut off with front switch like console
-everyone can have their own account
-can play old PC games on this (if updated as in GOG.com purchases)
-can upgrade memory and hard drive

CONS
-expensive(but very powerful for this price range)
-need to purchase keyboard and mouse for Windows operations
-Windows 8.1 can be a bit frustrating at times (Win 8.1 is not unique to this console, however)

THE BOTTOM LINE
When I first read about this console/PC unit, I thought it was way overpriced, but after using it, I REALLY like it so far. We have put this thing through constant use and pushing it since we got it. I have to say it is up to the task. My son who is an avid gamer and builds super computers is even impressed with it, which is saying a lot. In his opinion, it is a very powerful system for the price.

This is a PC designed for console gamers who might not really have discovered the world of PC gaming yet. It seems to be a solid machine that performs well. Working with Windows is not always an easy task, but in set up and basic gaming operations this system is really impressive to me.

WHO WOULD NOT WANT TO GET THIS SYSTEM
This is a high functioning computer that will run games on it and has a console experience attached with it. If you are just interested in using this for Steam, I would say that it is not worth the money. If you want to have a highly functioning Windows 8.1 system (capable of some great gaming) that allows you to have a console experience with Steam as an added bonus all on your TV, then this system is great.

UPDATE 6-2015
We are still crazy about this system. The more that we use it, the more fun it is to explore. The Alien Respawn takes a bit of messing with to get it to work right, but after the update, I finally got the system backed up.

The Steam console has been fun to use, although again, it is quirky when trying to use the Xbox 360 controller that we got with it. There is a glitch that causes some problems occasionally and has to be re-installed from time to time. I am not sure if it is a Windows 8.1 problem or a Steam problem. We are hoping to get the Steam controller when it comes out if it looks like a solid option.

We all have gotten and use Steam accounts and found it to work well so far. We are playing on Wi-Fi (not solid line in) and it still performs quite well.

All in all, this system is FANTASTIC and I can not recommend it highly enough. If I could give it TEN stars, I would.

And as silly as it seems, having the ability to change the colors on the alien head and the triangle shape thrills me to no end. Simple but fun.

Will update if we get the Steam controller to let you know how that works.
text_fidelity_b: Alienware Alpha ASM100-4980 Console (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I mounted mine on the hand rail of my apartment balcony, second floor and now receive all local channels 4-68. Channel 68 being about 45 miles away. All are received in full green in windows media center, without using a preamp.

Previously I had it mounted under and bolted to the 3rd floor balcony to try and keep it out of sight. Reception was iffy on 4 favorite channels. I then moved it to its' present location with the idea that the antennas footprint is considerably smaller than all the satellite dishes mounted on balconies throughout the complex. The mounting bracket and pole that come with it, are the same type satellite dishes use, Very strong and versatile. You will need to buy some good bolts, I used 4, 5/16" x 1- 1/2" Galvanized Lag and flat washers, I predrilled 3/16" pilot holes first. I just thought I'd mention that for those not fastener savvy.

I would guess the antenna mount alone is worth 1/3rd of the entire antenna cost. Recommend a good quad shield coaxial cable with the thick, sollid copper wire. A shorter run is better if possible. I only have about 12 feet to my PC/TV.

Once I figured out how to mount this antenna correctly, a month ago, I haven't had to adjust it.

text_fidelity_a:
Nexuslink Wave 2 G.hn Powerline Adapter | Pass-Through Outlet | 2000 Mbps I 2-Unit Kit I (GPL-2000PT-KIT) In terms of convenience, this is an outstanding product. It literally is plug and play. Just plug the transmitter in near you router and plug the Ethernet cable into an open port. Plug the receiver where you need the signal press the button on each device and setup is about complete. I had zero issues in terms of connection.

The farther the distance you span and the more walls and obstacles between, the slower the resultant signal will be. I tested the unit in a multitude of locations and I always received a signal, although it dropped the farther away I moved.

The point of this device is to use in locations where it is not possible, or where it would be difficult to run an Ethernet cable. If you are in a position where you need to get a signal to a TV to stream programming this would be a great choice. I tested it with Hulu, Prime and Netflix and it worked great. Depending on distance spanned and the strength of your original signal it probably would be adequate for internet use. However I can not recommend this as a viable option for gaming.

This set will definitely fulfill many people’s needs. It is just important to consider your use in relation to the WiFi product you install. For my family this worked fairly well.
text_fidelity_b: Nexuslink Wave 2 G.hn Powerline Adapter | Pass-Through Outlet | 2000 Mbps I 2-Unit Kit I (GPL-2000PT-KIT)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm I purchased this lens on Amazon offered by a gray market vendor for $140 (new!). Gray Market means there is no USA Warranty. I haven't tried to see if it is eligible, but I assume it would not be. As of this writing (10/12/2014), that vendor, CD Supply, is still offering the lens - though now for $170. Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.
text_fidelity_b: Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI)

As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

The ERGO still worked but would occasionally get stuck when the support pegs would catch the pock and cause the ball to resist - not enough to really hurt anything but just enough to make digital drawing difficult and just enough to annoy me. This replacement ball has taken care of that for me and has proven to be a worthwhile expense for me.

The ERGO and the M570 have the same size ball, so this ball can be used in either (I was using the ball from my old M570 in the ERGO while I waited for this ball to arrive). There are two different finish types available, glossy and matte. I chose the glossy in red. Operation has been absolutely smooth with no resistance at all and no catches. I haven’t noticed any operational differences between it and the original gray ball that came in my ERGO. And, in my opinion, the dark red of this ball actually looks a little nicer than the original silver ball as well as the blue M570 ball.

This wasn’t an expensive replacement and so far it has worked out very well for me. It has restored operation of my trackball to what it was before I damaged the original ball, which is really all I needed. Based on my experience with it, this is an easy replacement ball to recommend if you need to replace the ball in either a Logitech M570 or an MX ERGO.

text_fidelity_a:
Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black I have had this CPU fan now going on 5 months. I love this fan. I hadn't upgraded for nearly 10 years and decided on an AMD FM2 Black Edition 6300 6-core CPU with an MSI 970A-G43 Plus economy Micro Board and 16GB of Corsair Memory 4GBx4 in the 4 slots. I use my computer for gaming and all around use. I wanted a CPU cooler that would be quiet and still keep my cpu cool when I cranked it up for high-performance gaming. I found it with this AND it didn't break the bank. With the Turbo Clock OC setting it will idle down and bolt up to 4300mhz seamlessly while the fan moves from it's WHISPER silent 36c idle and general use, to it's 42c full bore o'clocked gaming use. The fan keeps it cool, and never does the fan become obtrusive or loud.

This fan is BIG. Don't even consider it if you have a micro or small mid-tower case. Your case must be generous in it's width to accommodate this cooler. Be sure to check the dimensions of your case with the unit. I have an older Antec 900 case it fit snugly into. I did have to remove the optional side window cooler intake fan I had installed with the prev board, cpu and cooler to allow it's fit. Also be sure your motherboard design placement of Memory slots is such that your Memory will clear it. My board's Corsair Vengence Memory JUST cleared it by a couple mm's laterally, and the top of the memory overtakes the bottom edge of cooler by about a quarter inch. If you are in the process of building your system a choice with low profile memory that doesn't have the tall heat spreaders would be a wise choice and safe bet if you are unsure about clearance with a board design that puts the memory slots very close to the CPU and cooler position. In the first photo attached I REVERSED the fan position to PULL the air thru on Left for best clearance instead of PUSHING the air through on the right if you just don't have the room, that flexibility is very handy. I wasn't satisfied with the cooling level and re-positioned the fan on right to PUSH it through later on and it sent the temps down a few more degrees. As you can see though in the second photo, it is much more snug.

Bottom line, a great cooler IF your case and build offers the room to fit it in. I would recommend it for those wanting great overclocking cooling performance and very quiet operation. I think most overclock enthusiasts would be well served to try this value priced solution before expensive and complicated water cooled solutions.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

text_fidelity_a:
museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.
text_fidelity_b: museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black

I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB connection to a computer, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 25ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a BIG plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series for a relatively inexpensive but high quality experience, or Bose if you are looking for something higher-end. The price of the Pioneer product is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately (about $70) and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price. Not great. Just ok.

Because this is basically the same as the "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone", and the other is about $70 cheaper, I would recommend getting the SBX10 and saving your money. They are basically the same thing, so either pay more and get better sound quality with another product entirely, or pay less for the same thing.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a:
Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27 We can not find the remote for our Roku or downstairs TV which is a Samsung since we had to remodel over a long period of time due to a flood which started it all. I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.
text_fidelity_b: Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27

I don't know if any of the other companies are better, but i've been a solid Canon customer for 20 years--as i told them--and I won't be anymore. text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire AIO Touch Desktop, 23.8" Full HD Touch, Intel Core i5-7400T, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, Windows 10 Home, AZ3-715-ACKi5 Computers are an important part of life. I know, I know- we need to get away from electronics and try to return to the days when more personal interactions were the norm. But regardless of how you feel about the proliferation of electronics in everyday living, there is no denying that most of us need them to one degree or another. We are writers/bloggers in my home and need good machines to carry us through the day. And the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop is one excellent machine for everyday use.

Let’s start with the physical attributes. This Acer computer features a very large flat screen with excellent clarity, making it ideal for watching videos, television shows, etc. The keyboard and mouse are wireless, so there is no issue over wires getting tangled as you work. Best of all, the CPU is part of the monitor. There is no separate tower or other computing unit, and that means this computer is space efficient. All you need is a place wide enough to handle the width of the monitor. The keyboard is certainly different from the one I was using previously and it took some adjusting to get used to. But this is the case with any new keyboard and you know what?- the adjustment period for this keyboard was less than a day. In almost no time at all, my wife and I took to the change and had no further issues.

As for the set up, well, it doesn’t get much better than this. I can remember when it would take several hours and much frustration to set up a new computer. But with Acer Aspire, the set up was complete and the computer was ready to use in less than 10 minutes after removing it from the box! We actually scheduled some time in our day, thinking it was going to require a fair amount of time to complete everything. It was so fast I started to worry that I did something wrong. But that wasn’t the case- everything is pretty much ready to go, straight from the package.

Because of our writing and blogging, we often need to have multiple windows open at any given time. This was an issue with my wife’s laptop and it would often slow her computer to a crawl. With this Acer computer, there is no such problem. She can have ten separate windows open, along with Microsoft Word and Excel, and the speed is still as good as ever. Again, this is a definite plus, as computer speed is a top concern for us and many other computer users.

I always try to find something that needs improvement when I write a product review but with the Acer Aspire, I can think of only one thing, and it relates to the Office Suite. They give you Office Suite for a free trial but once the trial is up, you will have to purchase it yourself. Acer could easily make this improvement and while this type of criticism has really nothing to do with the functionality of the product itself, it is about the only issue I can find. Everything else about this computer is well above average.

Computers are essential to my household. We need our computers for writing, for the classes I teach, and other uses. With the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop, we have found a cutting- edge computing machine that fits our needs perfectly and has everything we desire. It’s an excellent computer that would look really good on your desktop and I recommend it when it comes time for your next pc upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire AIO Touch Desktop, 23.8" Full HD Touch, Intel Core i5-7400T, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, Windows 10 Home, AZ3-715-ACKi5

VIZIO E700i-B3 70-Inch 1080p Smart LED HDTV I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. If you are using the actual remote rather than a universal one for the cable box, you have to aim directly at the very tiny eye in the far left bottom corner and it can take a couple of tries to hit it just right from across a big room. This drives me nuts when I'm streaming from Amazon Prime and need to pause the show quickly or try to flick through the selections. However, I would totally buy another Vizio tv again in the future if the new ones are as good as this two year old used one has been - I've definitely gotten my hundred fifty dollars worth out of this one.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO E700i-B3 70-Inch 1080p Smart LED HDTV

ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic) I knew the keyboard was red when I ordered it. I didn't know how bad that would suck, however. The keys are hard to read during the day. So you have no choice but to crank the backlight to max, wasting battery. Battery life is bad enough as it is. And the backlighting doesn't help much during the day. I just hate it.

Next issue is that it doesn't come with DVD playing software. Seriously? Why did I buy a computer with a DVD player in it? Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic)

I got this primarily for listening to music and ballgames through my I phone, via bluetooth. I Tunes App available for this product. Worked okay.

Things I didn't like.
1. Not stable on the shelf. While trying to understand the controls, it fell backwards with a light touch. No damage though. If it's not wall mounted, suggest you place support behind it. I Was fiddling with the controls trying to find the pair button, since I couldn't find it on the remote. Later, I found the pair button on the remote. Should have better support for shelf use.
2. Remote control is confusing. Must be paired each time you want to play via bluetooth, even when you don't shut the unit down. Instead of a pair button, the button says play menu. The small pamphlet does explain the functions on the remote. Not intuitive at all. Read the pamphlet.
3. Paired to my I phone easily enough, once I hit the pair button (on the radio, as well as the remote).
4. Although it paired easily to my I Phone, my I mac couldn't find the signal.
5. Weak FM. A few stations were fine, but I only picked up about 1/3 of the stations available. Not a real problem since I will stream via bluetooth.
6. No AM. I expected AM.
